Oblique

/uh-BLEEK/ - rhymes with sleek · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Oblique means indirect; not straightforward.

Tia's oblique postcard said only that the mountains 'ask nothing of anyone,' and the family understood she wasn't coming home soon.

Worked Example

The piano teacher never says a performance failed; her oblique verdict — 'the metronome missed you today' — sends students back to the practice room unasked.

Oblique means approaching at a slant instead of head-on: an oblique remark delivers its message while never stating it, leaving the listener to close the last step of the distance.

How Oblique Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

roundabout

roundabout: taking the long way to the point

sidelong

sidelong: delivered from the side, like a glance

Antonyms

direct

direct: aimed straight at the point

frank

frank: open and honest without softening

How Strong Is It? — diplomatic → oblique → veiled

diplomatic vs. oblique

diplomatic vs. oblique: Diplomatic is milder than oblique — the message is softened and cushioned, but it still arrives by the front door.

veiled vs. oblique

veiled vs. oblique: Veiled goes further than oblique: an oblique remark approaches from the side, while a veiled one hides its meaning almost entirely.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of oblique.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — ob-

Prefix — ob-: against, aslant

Root — lique

Root — lique: slanting (Latin obliquus)

Put it together

Put it together: Ob- (against, aslant) + lique (slanting, from Latin obliquus) = set at a slant. An oblique remark comes at its target from an angle instead of head-on.

Why there's no relative to spot

Why there's no relative to spot: Oblique is Latin obliquus, 'slanting.' The ob- ('against, aslant') is a familiar prefix, but the -liquus half survives in no other English word, so there is no cousin to peel off.

Strength Check

Word Choice

formal / literary

Oblique praises or accuses indirection, depending on who is speaking — oblique hints, oblique criticism, an oblique approach. Plain 'indirect' is flatter; oblique adds the sense of an angle chosen on purpose.
